# rtc-matrix-clock

<!-- Generated by tools/build-user-docs.py; edit tools/sketch-guides.json. -->

**Level:** Intermediate. No AI subscription or API key is needed.

[Start here](https://mikersays.github.io/agent-arduino/getting-started.html) · [Website instructions](https://mikersays.github.io/agent-arduino/sketches.html#rtc-matrix-clock) · [All sketches](../README.md)

## What you should see

A binary-coded clock displays hours, minutes, and seconds. The monitor prints the full date and time once a second.

## What you need

No external components; uses the built-in LEDs or matrix.

Install Arduino_RouterBridge with Library Manager. The UNO Q core supplies the board-specific headers.

## Upload this sketch

1. Complete the getting-started guide once to install the UNO Q core and libraries.
2. In Arduino IDE, open rtc-matrix-clock/rtc-matrix-clock.ino. Select Arduino UNO Q and its port.
3. Click Verify, then Upload. Uploading replaces the running microcontroller sketch.

Or, in the **UNO Q Linux terminal**, from the repository root:

```bash
python3 flash rtc-matrix-clock
```

Read the replacement prompt and enter `y` to compile and upload. To check compilation without uploading:

```bash
python3 flash rtc-matrix-clock --compile-only
```

The helper uploads locally on the board. For a computer-side IDE or network CLI upload, follow the getting-started guide.

## Try it

Read columns 1/2 for hours, 5/6 for minutes, and 9/10 for seconds (columns start at 0). From row 7 upward, bright bits are worth 1, 2, 4, and 8. Add them for each digit; ignore the dim baseline markers.

This sketch has no serial command controls. To change its behavior, edit the source, save, compile, and upload again.

## Limits and tips

When the RTC is not running, the sketch seeds it from compile time. An already running RTC is left alone. This is not internet time synchronization and has no serial SET command; rebuilding alone does not necessarily reset the clock.

## If it does not work

Compare the result with the expected behavior above, then follow [troubleshooting](https://mikersays.github.io/agent-arduino/getting-started.html#troubleshooting). Save your edits before downloading or uploading another version.

The repository records compilation with UNO Q core 0.56.0 on the original board. Typed serial input and most visual behavior still need hardware verification. These instructions describe the source code, not a new hardware test.

[Read the source](rtc-matrix-clock.ino) for the implementation and its original compile/upload commands.
